It’s another big week for British TV, but a particularly strong one for docs. From medical scandals and gruesome murder cases to a mockumentary that takes an irreverent look at the history of cinema, it's all set to be a fascinating viewing. Elsewhere, there’s the return of everyone’s favourite silly, soapy drama and a heist series featuring a much-loved British actor. Here’s our pick of the best of television to watch this week: Monday Mums vs Big Pharma BBC. The plight of the subpostmasters, sewage-polluted waterways and the contaminated blood scandal have all been the subject of TV documentaries and dramas recently, making for a damning picture of the UK government, health services and privatised utilities. Now there’s another scandal to add to the list. The anti-epileptic drug sodium valproate, commonly known as Epilim, was prescribed to pregnant women for decades despite known risks of severe birth defects and developmental disorders, echoing the thalidomide case of the 1950s. This documentary follows the heroic Janet Williams and Emma Murphy, whose children are among an estimated 20,000 affected by the drug. They fight for recognition and justice for those affected by conditions associated with exposure, including autism, learning difficulties and spina bifida. BBC2, 9pm Wednesday %0A%09%0A" width="60" height="60" alt="Play video"/> Rivals For all those who have been on tenterhooks for the second part of the second series of the soapy drama, your time is now. We join the horny gang of the fictional county of Rutshire as they attend Lady Monica’s funeral, following her death in the last episode when a tree fell on her car. However, the characters are back at their favourite pastime – shagging – within minutes. A fun, welcome return for stars including Danny Dyer, Aidan Turner and David Tennant. Disney+ What to Read Next Ken Loach Remembers Cathy Come Home Director Ken Loach reflects on the impact of his landmark 1966 drama, Cathy Come Home , about a couple’s decline into homelessness and poverty. Depressingly, it’s still relevant 60 years later. The TV film – which will be screened in full after the 15-minute interview with Loach – helped draw attention to homelessness around the time the charity Shelter was founded. It has since been called “the best television drama” of all time by Radio Times. BBC4, from 10pm. View full post on YouTube Hunting Alice Bell This crime drama, created by David Baddiel and Peter Bradshaw, focuses on Fran Da Silva, a leisure centre employee whose life is turned upside down when an online vigilante mob accuses her of being Alice Bell. Alice was the lover and accomplice of a notorious serial killer and anaesthetist, and has since been given a new identity under witness protection. Starring Simon Pegg as the serial killer and Alexandra Roach as Fran. Channel 4, 9pm Thursday %0A%09%0A" width="60" height="60" alt="Play video"/> Cunk on Cinema Philomena Cunk (Diane Morgan) is back and she’s got a lot of questions, but mainly: where did cinema come from? There are more hilarious deadpan discoveries from Cunk in this Charlie Brooker-helmed mockumentary, alongside appearances from directors, editors and composers who work in the hallowed halls of Hollywood and beyond. Benedict Cumberbatch even joins in the fun, too. Here’s hoping she investigates how cinemas can get away with such a big mark-up on popcorn. BBC2, 10pm, BBC iPlayer and Netflix. The Jigsaw Puzzle Murderer Even true-crime fans will be shocked by the gruesome nature of this two-part documentary. Back in 2024, a dismembered human torso was found in the woods near Salford, and further grisly discoveries awaited Greater Manchester Police as they investigated the murder of Stuart Everett. This series interviews the detectives at the heart of the case, revealing the full, horrifying story. Paramount+. Friday %0A%09%0A" width="60" height="60" alt="Play video"/> 12 12 12 A Christmas Eve heist thriller starring Jamie Dornan and Anthony Mackie? Yes, please. Dornan plays Paul Galvin, a criminal who, in time-honoured fashion, is doing “one last job” before settling down to a quiet life of marriage and children. But hot on his tail is FBI agent Jack Strickland (Mackie), who’s hoping to intercept him during the 12 months it takes to plan the robbery, the 12 hours of the heist itself and the 12 days of the police investigation – hence the title of the series.
